name: Hue Bridge Pro (EU)

radios.note: Philips lists Zigbee and Bluetooth, and says the Pro joins the router by Wi-Fi or the included Ethernet cable (Ethernet recommended). The spec line 'works without Wi-Fi' means a Wi-Fi link isn't required.

matter.note: CSA lists the 'Hue Bridge Matter Platform' (Signify, Matter 1.4.2, January 2026), a software component on 'Hue Bridge version 3' that shows and links to the Bridge Pro and bridges Ethernet and Zigbee. The Pro can also join by Wi-Fi.

apple_home.note: Apple Home is listed on the EU page; Matter also works through the bridge.

google_home.note: Google Home is listed on the EU page; Matter also works through the bridge.

alexa.note: Amazon Alexa is listed on the EU page; Matter also works through the bridge.

smartthings.note: Samsung SmartThings is listed on the EU page.

home_assistant.note: Through Home Assistant's Matter integration, which names the Philips Hue Bridge as a Matter bridge. Home Assistant's Hue integration page names only V1 and V2 bridges, not the Pro, so native support isn't confirmed.

localControl.note: Not confirmed. Philips says some AI-based features can run on the hub without relying solely on the cloud.

deviceProtocols.note: Hue lights and accessories over Zigbee.

matterBridge.note: Philips says Matter works through the bridge; check Philips for which Hue products pass through.

threadBorderRouter.note: Philips's pages don't mention Thread for the Bridge Pro. A Matter Alpha page calls it a Matter border router, which is not a Thread claim.

maxDevices.note: Philips gives two separate limits: 150+ lights and 50+ accessories, so no single number is recorded.

summary: Hue Bridge Pro (EU, EAN 8720169155114) takes 150+ lights and 50+ accessories, by Philips' count. Hue devices talk Zigbee to it, and it connects to your router by Ethernet (recommended) or Wi-Fi. Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings are listed on Philips' EU page, and Matter works through the bridge, which is how Home Assistant gets it.
caveats: Philips lists the limits as 150+ lights and 50+ accessories, not one total.
Home Assistant support is through Matter; its Hue integration page names only V1 and V2 bridges, not the Pro.
Philips doesn't mention Thread for the Bridge Pro, so don't count on it as a Thread border router.
